ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure is a curve of speed speed(rpm) versus torque torque(Nm). The vertical axis is marked with 1500 rpm and 1400 rpm, and the horizontal axis is marked with 0 and 5 Nm. The solid line descends toward the lower right from about 0 Nm, 1500 rpm, to 5 Nm, 1400 rpm; the dashed auxiliary lines mark the intersection of 1400 rpm and 5 Nm. Reasoning: The excitation voltage is kept at the rated value, so the magnetic flux is approximately constant, the DC motor back EMF E is proportional to the speed n, and the electromagnetic torque T is proportional to the armature current I_a. The problem ignores rotational losses, and the no-load torque is 0, so the no-load armature current is approximately 0; under 1500 rpm and 200 V armature voltage, the back EMF E_1500 = 200 V. Therefore, at 1400 rpm, the back EMF is E_1400 = 200 × (1400/1500) = 186.67 V. It is known that at 1400 rpm and output torque 5 Nm, the armature voltage is still 200 V, so the armature resistance voltage drop corresponding to 5 Nm is I_a R_a = 200 - 186.67 = 13.33 V. Since torque is proportional to armature current, when the torque is 2.5 Nm, the current is half of that at 5 Nm, so the armature resistance voltage drop is also half, namely 6.67 V. In order to output 2.5 Nm at 1400 rpm, the required armature voltage is V_a = E_1400 + I_a R_a = 186.67 + 6.67 = 193.33 V.

raw_record.question_text:
A separately excited DC motor runs at 1500 rpm under no-load with 200 V applied to the armature. The field voltage is maintained at its rated value. The speed of the motor, when it delivers a torque of 5 Nm, is 1400 rpm, as shown in the figure. The rotational losses and armature reaction are neglected.

For the motor to deliver a torque of 2.5 Nm at 1400 rpm, the armature voltage to be applied is ______.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: it shows a speed-versus-torque line passing through 1500 rpm at 0 Nm and 1400 rpm at 5 Nm. From the text, the 0 Nm, 1500 rpm point occurs with 200 V armature voltage and rated constant field. Therefore the back emf at 1500 rpm is 200 V. At 1400 rpm, back emf is 200*(1400/1500). For the known 5 Nm point at 1400 rpm with 200 V applied, the armature resistance drop equals 200 - 200*(1400/1500). Since torque is proportional to armature current, the resistance drop at 2.5 Nm is half of the 5 Nm drop. Add this half-drop to the 1400-rpm back emf to get the required armature voltage, yielding about 193.3 V.

图像描述：附图是转速 speed(rpm) 对转矩 torque(Nm) 的曲线。纵轴标有 1500 rpm 和 1400 rpm，横轴标有 0 和 5 Nm。实线从约 0 Nm、1500 rpm 处向右下方下降，到 5 Nm、1400 rpm 处；虚线辅助线标出了 1400 rpm 和 5 Nm 的交点。

method.method_draft: First describe the image: it is a straight speed-torque graph with intercept 1500 rpm at zero torque and a marked point of 1400 rpm at 5 Nm. From this, infer the 200 V characteristic has a speed drop of 20 rpm per Nm. At 2.5 Nm, the same motor would have a torque drop of 50 rpm from its no-load-speed intercept. To make the operating speed 1400 rpm at 2.5 Nm, the required no-load-speed intercept must therefore be 1400 + 50 = 1450 rpm. Since no-load speed is proportional to armature voltage under constant field, scale the voltage from the original no-load point: V = 200*(1450/1500) = 193.3 V.
method.CoT_raw:
Image description: The attached image shows a speed–torque graph for the DC motor. The vertical axis is speed in rpm and the horizontal axis is torque in Nm. The straight descending line starts at 1500 rpm at zero torque and reaches the marked operating point of 1400 rpm at 5 Nm, indicated by dashed guide lines.

Reasoning: For the 200 V armature-voltage characteristic, the speed drop from no-load to 5 Nm is 1500 - 1400 = 100 rpm. Hence the speed drop per unit torque is 100/5 = 20 rpm per Nm. At 2.5 Nm, the speed drop on a parallel characteristic is therefore 2.5 × 20 = 50 rpm. To have the actual speed equal to 1400 rpm at 2.5 Nm, the required no-load speed intercept must be 1400 + 50 = 1450 rpm. With field voltage maintained constant, no-load speed is proportional to armature voltage. Therefore, V = 200 × (1450/1500) = 193.33 V.
